div.div:
Plain objects. Thrown away and rebuilt on every render — creating them is cheap.
This is what JSX compiles to.

div.div:
Persistent. Survives renders and holds your state, your hooks and the work still to do.
A linked list, not a call stack — so React can pause.

Real nodes. The only tree the browser paints, and the expensive one to touch.
Mutated only in the commit phase.

div.div: Why the middle tree exists

div.style: display: flex; align-items: unsafe center; justify-content: unsafe flex-start; width: 338px; height: 1px; padding-top: 385px; margin-left: 58px;
box-sizing: border-box; font-size: 0; text-align: left; color: var(--dg-bad-fg);

div.div: Without fibers (the old stack reconciler) rendering was one recursive call. Once it started it ran to the end — a 3,000-row list froze the tab.

div.style: display: flex; align-items: unsafe center; justify-content: unsafe flex-start; width: 340px; height: 1px; padding-top: 385px; margin-left: 438px;
box-sizing: border-box; font-size: 0; text-align: left; color: var(--dg-ok-fg);

display: inline-block; font-size: 11px; font-family: 'IBM Plex Sans',-apple-system,BlinkMacSystemFont,'Segoe UI',Roboto,sans-serif; color: var(--dg-ok-fg); line-height: 1.2; pointer-events: all; white-space: normal; word-wrap: normal;

div.div: With fibers the work is a list of units React owns. It can do some, yield to a click, and resume — or throw the half-done tree away.

div.style: display: flex; align-items: unsafe center; justify-content: unsafe flex-start; width: 732px; height: 1px; padding-top: 442px; margin-left: 46px;
box-sizing: border-box; font-size: 0; text-align: left; color: var(--dg-fg);

display: inline-block; font-size: 11px; font-family: 'IBM Plex Sans',-apple-system,BlinkMacSystemFont,'Segoe UI',Roboto,sans-serif; color: var(--dg-fg); line-height: 1.2; pointer-events: all; white-space: normal; word-wrap: normal;

div.div: Two fiber trees exist at once: current (on screen) and work-in-progress (being built). alternate links each node to its twin, and committing is a pointer swap — which is why a render that is thrown away costs nothing on screen.

div.style: display: flex; align-items: unsafe center; justify-content: unsafe flex-start; width: 756px; height: 1px; padding-top: 513px; margin-left: 40px;
box-sizing: border-box; font-size: 0; text-align: left; color: var(--dg-warn-fg);

display: inline-block; font-size: 12px; font-family: 'IBM Plex Sans',-apple-system,BlinkMacSystemFont,'Segoe UI',Roboto,sans-serif; color: var(--dg-warn-fg); line-height: 1.2; pointer-events: all; white-space: normal; word-wrap: normal;

div.div: State lives on the fiber, not in your component. That is why a component function can run twice and still see one state.
